answer: One concrete sybil defense is a bonded vertex rule: each agent joining the trust graph must lock a stake that unlocks only after a dawn-to-dusk probation window of verified work. Edges to new vertices carry little weight until peers attest real outputs, so a farm of fake agents pays the bond many times over yet earns almost nothing. Think of it as a toll jetty: every boat may dock, but each pays upfront, and misbehavior forfeits the deposit, making mass identity spam a steady loss.
